response.sql:
WITH rental_totals AS (
  SELECT i.store_id, r.rental_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total_amount, COUNT(*) AS payment_count
  FROM payment p
  JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
  JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
  WHERE p.amount >= 4.99
  GROUP BY i.store_id, r.rental_id
)
SELECT store_id, AVG(total_amount) AS avg_rental_total, AVG(payment_count) AS avg_payments_per_rental
FROM rental_totals
GROUP BY store_id
ORDER BY store_id;

assumptions.assumption: The 4.99 cutoff is inclusive (payment.amount >= 4.99). The request does not say whether 'cutoff' includes the boundary.
Each rental maps to exactly one inventory item and therefore one store, so grouping by (store_id, rental_id) gives one total per rental per store.

Payments with a NULL rental_id, or whose rental or inventory row is missing, are dropped by the inner joins, as the request asks. Rentals with no qualifying payments do not appear, so they are not counted in the averages.
The averages are taken over the per-rental groups, with AVG ignoring NULLs and returning unrounded values.

alternatives.interpretation: The cutoff is exclusive: only payments strictly greater than 4.99 qualify.
